condition.narrative: ESCP, 1.2: Asbestos Management Plan shall be prepared, consulted upon, disclosed, and adopted prior to commencement of demolitionof an existing facility for the construction of the Land Administration Building.
ESCP, 10.2: Setting up of GRM to be undertaken within 60 days of project effectiveness.

Schedule 2, Section I, A.2 (a): The Recipient shall not later than sixty (60) days of the Effective Date, establish a steeringcommittee (“Project Steering Committee), and thereafter, maintain, throughout the period of Project implementation said steeringcommittee with mandate, composition, and resources, satisfactory to the Association (“Project Steering Committee”).

Schedule 2, Section I, A.3 (b)(ii): The Recipient shall not later than sixty (60) days of the Effective Date, recruit andthereafter maintain a monitoring and evaluation specialist, a financial management assistant, a procurement assistant, a trainingcoordinator, all in accordance with the Procurement Regulations

Schedule 2, Section I, A.4(a):The Recipient shall within sixty (60) days of the Effective Date, establish the Project TechnicalCommittee with terms of reference and functions, satisfactory to the Association, and thereafter, maintain throughout Projectimplementation said Project Technical Committee with the responsibility for providing technical advice.

Schedule 2, Section I, A.4(b)(i):The Recipient shall maintain throughout Project implementation the VGGT technical working groupand the inter-ministerial task force with terms of reference and functions, satisfactory to the Association, and to support landreforms within the context of the VGGT implementation framework.

Schedule 2, Section I, A.4(b)(ii):The Recipient shall maintain throughout Project implementation the MLHCP and Office of theAdministrator and Registrar General Working Group with terms of reference and functions, satisfactory to the Association, and withthe responsibility for coordination in lead MDAs on administration of land processes and guiding the transitional arrangements thatwill be required if the proposed National Land Commission Bill is enacted

title.narrative: Land offices built or renovated at the central and provincial level that incorporate resilient design principles, are staffed and operational

comment.narrative:
The indicator measure the number of land offices renovated or constructed based on climate resilient designs, that are staffed in line with respective guidelines, and operational with required furniture and equipment.
Status: The architectural firm finalizing the design for the NLC Headquarters and District Offices. The PCU is also making good progress with the preparation of the site-specific ESMPs. The focus is on promptly finalizing the design stage of the NLC offices, preparing the Asbestos Management Plan for the Freetown site, and launching the tender of the contracts for the construction stage by April 2025.

title.narrative: Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) installed and operational

comment.narrative:
The indicator measure how many CORS have been installed and made functional to form the geodetic network.
Status: MLHCP signed the contract with AIOS/METAMINDS for the Design, Supply and Installation of Continuous Operating Reference Stations (CORS). The inception phase was completed. Following the site reconnaissance, the contractor has proposed a switch to Starlink and an expansion of the CORS network. The proposal is being reviewed by the World Bank.

title.narrative: People with use or ownership rights recorded

comment.narrative:
The indicator measures the number of people whose land rights are recorded and/or registered as a result of the project - either individually, jointly with spouses/partners, or as part of a family. This include land records that have been corrected and it will include properties that are registered for the first time.
Status: Procurement of a firm to assist the project with systematic registration of land is progressing and expected to be mobilized by Novembre 2024.

title.narrative: Chiefdom Land Committees and Town or Village Land Committees in project area with at least 30% female membership

comment.narrative:
The indicator will measure how many local land committees have been established in accordance with the legal gender provisions.
Status: â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹Project target districts encompass 266 chiefdoms and over 7,000 towns/villages. Two Chiefdom Land Committees and 292 Town/Village Land Committees have been established. The plan is to establish the remaining ones by the end of January 2025.

The indicator will measure the number of MLHCP, OARG and other government staff as well as private sector land specialists and CSO staff that are trained in surveying, land registration, land dispute resolution, etc. as well as administrative disciplines like general office administration and management, procurement, M&E, etc.
Status:â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹ A training needs assessment was completed and a training plan was prepared for 2024. The PIU will start reporting actual figures by the end of 2024/2025.

Status: â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹â€‹ First drafts of the Land Title Registration Act, Land Adjudication, and the Survey Act have been prepared. New drafts were shared in October 2024 and are being reviewed.

title.narrative: Chiefdom Land Committees and Town or Village Land Committees in project area with at least 30% female membership

comment.narrative:
The indicator will measure how many local land committees have been established in accordance with the legal gender provisions.
Status: Land committees have been established in 8 chiefdoms and 1,626 villages and towns. There are 68 chiefdoms, and an estimated 6,783 towns and villages in the SLLAP target districts of Kenema, Port Loko, Makeni, Bo, and Bonthe.

The indicator will measure the number of land laws submitted to Parliament, e.g. Land Surveying Bill and Land Title Registration Bill (the legal assessment will determine which bills the project would prioritize and measure)
Status:  Two Land Laws have been enacted, namely the National Land Commission (2022) and the Customary Land Rights Act (2022). The government is currently working on the Land Title Registration Act, Land Adjudication, and the Survey Act. The most recent versions of these Acts have been shared with the World Bank, and are intended to be submitted to Parliament by April 2025.
Status: The number of transactions reported is only from OARG's Office in the provinces. The PCU and NLC are working with OARG to obtain the data for Freetown

title.narrative: Time to complete the registration of a transaction of a land parcel in the land administration system

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the time it takes within the land administration system to register a land transaction. The indicator only measures the time that government staff spend on a transaction. Delays caused by customers (i.e. in case of incomplete documents being submitted) are not measured.
Status: Business process re-engineering will result in the design of more efficient processes. An initial study was conducted and will be finalized by the consultancy firm under component 3. These processes will be reflected in the land information system, for which the tender is ongoing.
